entry.title: Chaos control with broken symmetries
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03480-4 By breaking both material and cavity symmetries, waves can be funnelled into robust closed-loop patterns. This dual-symmetry-breaking approach enables the development of a new class of devices for wave-based signal processing and sensing.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics

entry.title: Cavity-less Brillouin strong coupling in a solid-state continuous system
entry.summary:
Nature Physics, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03458-2 Strong coupling between light and matter is typically realized in resonators. Now it is shown that this can happen in a cavity-less waveguide scenario in which the light passes through only once.

Source: Nature Physics · Tags: #quantum-physics #optics-photonics

entry.title: Photonic circuits become trainable AI hardware
entry.summary:
Nature Computational Science, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s43588-026-01071-0 A physics-based in situ learning method is demonstrated that directly measures optical gradients with photonic integrated circuits, allowing diverse circuit topologies to be trained after fabrication.
